NKJV.1: “When a man takes a wife and marries her, and it happens that she finds no favor in his eyes because he has found some uncleanness in her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand, and sends her out of his house,
NKJV.2: when she has departed from his house, and goes and becomes another man’s wife,
NKJV.3: if the latter husband detests her and writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand, and sends her out of his house, or if the latter husband dies who took her as his wife,
NKJV.4: then her former husband who divorced her must not take her back to be his wife after she has been defiled; for that is an abomination before the LORD, and you shall not bring sin on the land which the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
NKJV.5: “When a man has taken a new wife, he shall not go out to war or be charged with any business; he shall be free at home one year, and bring happiness to his wife whom he has taken.
NKJV.6: “No man shall take the lower or the upper millstone in pledge, for he takes one’s living in pledge.
NKJV.7: “If a man is found kidnapping any of his brethren of the children of Israel, and mistreats him or sells him, then that kidnapper shall die; and you shall put away the evil from among you.
NKJV.8: “Take heed in an outbreak of leprosy, that you carefully observe and do according to all that the priests, the Levites, shall teach you; just as I commanded them, so you shall be careful to do.
NKJV.9: Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the way when you came out of Egypt!
NKJV.10: “When you lend your brother anything, you shall not go into his house to get his pledge.
NKJV.11: You shall stand outside, and the man to whom you lend shall bring the pledge out to you.
NKJV.12: And if the man is poor, you shall not keep his pledge overnight.
NKJV.13: You shall in any case return the pledge to him again when the sun goes down, that he may sleep in his own garment and bless you; and it shall be righteousness to you before the LORD your God.
NKJV.14: “You shall not oppress a hired servant who is poor and needy, whether one of your brethren or one of the aliens who is in your land within your gates.
NKJV.15: Each day you shall give him his wages, and not let the sun go down on it, for he is poor and has set his heart on it; lest he cry out against you to the LORD, and it be sin to you.
NKJV.16: “Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor shall children be put to death for their fathers; a person shall be put to death for his own sin.
NKJV.17: “You shall not pervert justice due the stranger or the fatherless, nor take a widow’s garment as a pledge.
NKJV.18: But you shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you from there; therefore I command you to do this thing.
NKJV.19: “When you reap your harvest in your field, and forget a sheaf in the field, you shall not go back to get it; it shall be for the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow, that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
NKJV.20: When you beat your olive trees, you shall not go over the boughs again; it shall be for the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow.
NKJV.21: When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you shall not glean it afterward; it shall be for the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow.
NKJV.22: And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt; therefore I command you to do this thing.

ESV.1: “When a man takes a wife and marries her, if then she finds no favor in his eyes because he has found some indecency in her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce and puts it in her hand and sends her out of his house, and she departs out of his house,
ESV.2: and if she goes and becomes another man's wife,
ESV.3: and the latter man hates her and writes her a certificate of divorce and puts it in her hand and sends her out of his house, or if the latter man dies, who took her to be his wife,
ESV.4: then her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after she has been defiled, for that is an abomination before the LORD. And you shall not bring sin upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you for an inheritance.
ESV.5: “When a man is newly married, he shall not go out with the army or be liable for any other public duty. He shall be free at home one year to be happy with his wife  whom he has taken.
ESV.6: “No one shall take a mill or an upper millstone in pledge, for that would be taking a life in pledge.
ESV.7: “If a man is found stealing one of his brothers of the people of Israel, and if he treats him as a slave or sells him, then that thief shall die. So you shall purge the evil from your midst.
ESV.8: “Take care, in a case of leprous  disease, to be very careful to do according to all that the Levitical priests shall direct you. As I commanded them, so you shall be careful to do.
ESV.9: Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the way as you came out of Egypt.
ESV.10: “When you make your neighbor a loan of any sort, you shall not go into his house to collect his pledge.
ESV.11: You shall stand outside, and the man to whom you make the loan shall bring the pledge out to you.
ESV.12: And if he is a poor man, you shall not sleep in his pledge.
ESV.13: You shall restore to him the pledge as the sun sets, that he may sleep in his cloak and bless you. And it shall be righteousness for you before the LORD your God.
ESV.14: “You shall not oppress a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether he is one of your brothers or one of the sojourners who are in your land within your towns.
ESV.15: You shall give him his wages on the same day, before the sun sets (for he is poor and counts on it), lest he cry against you to the LORD, and you be guilty of sin.
ESV.16: “Fathers shall not be put to death because of their children, nor shall children be put to death because of their fathers. Each one shall be put to death for his own sin.
ESV.17: “You shall not pervert the justice due to the sojourner or to the fatherless, or take a widow's garment in pledge,
ESV.18: but you shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you from there; therefore I command you to do this.
ESV.19: “When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in the field, you shall not go back to get it. It shall be for the sojourner, the fatherless, and the widow, that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
ESV.20: When you beat your olive trees, you shall not go over them again. It shall be for the sojourner, the fatherless, and the widow.
ESV.21: When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you shall not strip it afterward. It shall be for the sojourner, the fatherless, and the widow.
ESV.22: You shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt; therefore I command you to do this.

NASB.1: 'When a man takes a wife and marries her, and it happens that she finds no favor in his eyes because he has found some indecency in her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce and puts [it] in her hand and sends her out from his house,
NASB.2: and she leaves his house and goes and becomes another man's [wife],
NASB.3: and if the latter husband turns against her and writes her a certificate of divorce and puts [it] in her hand and sends her out of his house, or if the latter husband dies who took her to be his wife,
NASB.4: [then] her former husband who sent her away is not allowed to take her again to be his wife, since she has been defiled; for that is an abomination before the LORD, and you shall not bring sin on the land which the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance.
NASB.5: 'When a man takes a new wife, he shall not go out with the army nor be charged with any duty; he shall be free at home one year and shall give happiness to his wife whom he has taken.
NASB.6: 'No one shall take a handmill or an upper millstone in pledge, for he would be taking a life in pledge.
NASB.7: 'If a man is caught kidnapping any of his countrymen of the sons of Israel, and he deals with him violently or sells him, then that thief shall die; so you shall purge the evil from among you.
NASB.8: 'Be careful against an infection of leprosy, that you diligently observe and do according to all that the Levitical priests teach you; as I have commanded them, so you shall be careful to do.
NASB.9: 'Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the way as you came out of Egypt.
NASB.10: 'When you make your neighbor a loan of any sort, you shall not enter his house to take his pledge.
NASB.11: 'You shall remain outside, and the man to whom you make the loan shall bring the pledge out to you.
NASB.12: 'If he is a poor man, you shall not sleep with his pledge.
NASB.13: 'When the sun goes down you shall surely return the pledge to him, that he may sleep in his cloak and bless you; and it will be righteousness for you before the LORD your God.
NASB.14: 'You shall not oppress a hired servant [who is] poor and needy, whether [he is] one of your countrymen or one of your aliens who is in your land in your towns.
NASB.15: 'You shall give him his wages on his day before the sun sets, for he is poor and sets his heart on it; so that he will not cry against you to the LORD and it become sin in you.
NASB.16: 'Fathers shall not be put to death for [their] sons, nor shall sons be put to death for [their] fathers; everyone shall be put to death for his own sin.
NASB.17: 'You shall not pervert the justice due an alien [or] an orphan, nor take a widow's garment in pledge.
NASB.18: 'But you shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and that the LORD your God redeemed you from there; therefore I am commanding you to do this thing.
NASB.19: 'When you reap your harvest in your field and have forgotten a sheaf in the field, you shall not go back to get it; it shall be for the alien, for the orphan, and for the widow, in order that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
NASB.20: 'When you beat your olive tree, you shall not go over the boughs again; it shall be for the alien, for the orphan, and for the widow.
NASB.21: 'When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you shall not go over it again; it shall be for the alien, for the orphan, and for the widow.
NASB.22: 'You shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt; therefore I am commanding you to do this thing.

CSB17.1: “If a man marries a woman, but she becomes displeasing to him <sup>[1]</sup> because he finds something indecent about her, he may write her a divorce certificate, hand it to her, and send her away from his house. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.2: If after leaving his house she goes and becomes another man’s wife,
CSB17.3: and the second man hates her, writes her a divorce certificate, hands it to her, and sends her away from his house or if he dies,
CSB17.4: the first husband who sent her away may not marry her again after she has been defiled, because that would be detestable to the LORD. You must not bring guilt on the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.5: “When a man takes a bride, he must not go out with the army or be liable for any duty. He is free to stay at home for one year, so that he can bring joy to the wife he has married.
CSB17.6: “Do not take a pair of grindstones or even the upper millstone as security for a debt, because that is like taking a life as security.
CSB17.7: “If a man is discovered kidnapping <sup>ⓜ</sup> one of his Israelite brothers, whether he treats him as a slave or sells him, the kidnapper must die. You must purge the evil from you.
CSB17.8: “Be careful with a person who has a case of serious skin disease, following carefully everything the Levitical priests instruct you to do. Be careful to do as I have commanded them.
CSB17.9: Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the journey after you left Egypt. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.10: “When you make a loan of any kind to your neighbor, do not enter his house to collect what he offers as security.
CSB17.11: Stand outside while the man you are making the loan to brings the security out to you.
CSB17.12: If he is a poor man, do not sleep with the garment he has given as security.
CSB17.13: Be sure to return it <sup>[2]</sup> to him at sunset. Then he will sleep in it and bless you, and this will be counted as righteousness to you before the LORD your God. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.14: “Do not oppress a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether one of your Israelite brothers or one of the resident aliens in a town <sup>[3]</sup> in your land.
CSB17.15: You are to pay him his wages each day before the sun sets, because he is poor and depends on them. <sup>ⓑ</sup> Otherwise he will cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be held guilty.
CSB17.16: “Fathers are not to be put to death for their children, and children are not to be put to death for their fathers; each person will be put to death for his own sin. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.17: Do not deny justice to a resident alien or fatherless child, and do not take a widow’s garment as security.
CSB17.18: Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed <sup>ⓓ</sup> you from there. Therefore I am commanding you to do this. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.19: “When you reap the harvest in your field, and you forget a sheaf in the field, do not go back to get it. It is to be left for the resident alien, the fatherless, and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.20: When you knock down the fruit from your olive tree, do not go over the branches again. What remains will be for the resident alien, the fatherless, and the widow.
CSB17.21: When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, do not glean what is left. What remains will be for the resident alien, the fatherless, and the widow.
CSB17.22: Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt. Therefore I am commanding you to do this. <sup>ⓖ</sup>

NLT.1: “Suppose a man marries a woman but she does not please him. Having discovered something wrong with her, he writes a document of divorce, hands it to her, and sends her away from his house.
NLT.2: When she leaves his house, she is free to marry another man.
NLT.3: But if the second husband also turns against her, writes a document of divorce, hands it to her, and sends her away, or if he dies,
NLT.4: the first husband may not marry her again, for she has been defiled. That would be detestable to the LORD. You must not bring guilt upon the land the LORD your God is giving you as a special possession.
NLT.5: “A newly married man must not be drafted into the army or be given any other official responsibilities. He must be free to spend one year at home, bringing happiness to the wife he has married.
NLT.6: “It is wrong to take a set of millstones, or even just the upper millstone, as security for a loan, for the owner uses it to make a living.
NLT.7: “If anyone kidnaps a fellow Israelite and treats him as a slave or sells him, the kidnapper must die. In this way, you will purge the evil from among you.
NLT.8: “In all cases involving serious skin diseases, be careful to follow the instructions of the Levitical priests; obey all the commands I have given them.
NLT.9: Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam as you were coming from Egypt.
NLT.10: “If you lend anything to your neighbor, do not enter his house to pick up the item he is giving as security.
NLT.11: You must wait outside while he goes in and brings it out to you.
NLT.12: If your neighbor is poor and gives you his cloak as security for a loan, do not keep the cloak overnight.
NLT.13: Return the cloak to its owner by sunset so he can stay warm through the night and bless you, and the LORD your God will count you as righteous.
NLT.14: “Never take advantage of poor and destitute laborers, whether they are fellow Israelites or foreigners living in your towns.
NLT.15: You must pay them their wages each day before sunset because they are poor and are counting on it. If you don’t, they might cry out to the LORD against you, and it would be counted against you as sin.
NLT.16: “Parents must not be put to death for the sins of their children, nor children for the sins of their parents. Those deserving to die must be put to death for their own crimes.
NLT.17: “True justice must be given to foreigners living among you and to orphans, and you must never accept a widow’s garment as security for her debt.
NLT.18: Always remember that you were slaves in Egypt and that the LORD your God redeemed you from your slavery. That is why I have given you this command.
NLT.19: “When you are harvesting your crops and forget to bring in a bundle of grain from your field, don’t go back to get it. Leave it for the foreigners, orphans, and widows. Then the LORD your God will bless you in all you do.
NLT.20: When you beat the olives from your olive trees, don’t go over the boughs twice. Leave the remaining olives for the foreigners, orphans, and widows.
NLT.21: When you gather the grapes in your vineyard, don’t glean the vines after they are picked. Leave the remaining grapes for the foreigners, orphans, and widows.
NLT.22: Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt. That is why I am giving you this command.

WEB.1: When a man takes a wife and marries her, then it shall be, if she finds no favor in his eyes, because he has found some unseemly thing in her, that he shall write her a bill of divorce, and put it in her hand, and send her out of his house.
WEB.2: When she has departed out of his house, she may go and be another man’s wife.
WEB.3: If the latter husband hates her, and write her a bill of divorce, and puts it in her hand, and sends her out of his house; or if the latter husband die, who took her to be his wife;
WEB.4: her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after that she is defiled; for that is abomination before Yahweh. You shall not cause the land to sin, which Yahweh your God gives you for an inheritance.
WEB.5: When a man takes a new wife, he shall not go out in the army, neither shall he be assigned any business. He shall be free at home one year, and shall cheer his wife whom he has taken.
WEB.6: No man shall take the mill or the upper millstone as a pledge; for he takes a life in pledge.
WEB.7: If a man is found stealing any of his brothers of the children of Israel, and he deals with him as a slave, or sells him; then that thief shall die. So you shall remove the evil from among you.
WEB.8: Be careful in the plague of leprosy, that you observe diligently, and do according to all that the priests the Levites teach you. As I commanded them, so you shall observe to do.
WEB.9: Remember what Yahweh your God did to Miriam, by the way as you came out of Egypt.
WEB.10: When you lend your neighbor any kind of loan, you shall not go into his house to get his pledge.
WEB.11: You shall stand outside, and the man to whom you lend shall bring the pledge outside to you.
WEB.12: If he is a poor man, you shall not sleep with his pledge.
WEB.13: You shall surely restore to him the pledge when the sun goes down, that he may sleep in his garment, and bless you. It shall be righteousness to you before Yahweh your God.
WEB.14: You shall not oppress a hired servant who is poor and needy, whether he is one of your brothers, or one of the foreigners who are in your land within your gates.
WEB.15: In his day you shall give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down on it; for he is poor, and sets his heart on it; lest he cry against you to Yahweh, and it be sin to you.
WEB.16: The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers. Every man shall be put to death for his own sin.
WEB.17: You shall not deprive the foreigner or the fatherless of justice, nor take a widow’s clothing in pledge;
WEB.18: but you shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and Yahweh your God redeemed you there. Therefore I command you to do this thing.
WEB.19: When you reap your harvest in your field, and have forgotten a sheaf in the field, you shall not go again to get it. It shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow; that Yahweh your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
WEB.20: When you beat your olive tree, you shall not go over the boughs again. It shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
WEB.21: When you harvest your vineyard, you shall not glean it after yourselves. It shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
WEB.22: You shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt. Therefore I command you to do this thing.

AMP.4: then her former husband who [first] sent her away may not take her again as his wife, since she has been defiled; for that is an outrage before the LORD, and you shall not bring sin on the land which the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance.

MSG.1: If a man marries a woman and then it happens that he no longer likes her because he has found something wrong with her, he may give her divorce papers, put them in her hand, and send her off.
MSG.2: After she leaves, if she becomes another man's wife
MSG.3: and he also comes to hate her and this second husband also gives her divorce papers, puts them in her hand, and sends her off, or if he should die,
MSG.4: then the first husband who divorced her can't marry her again. She has made herself ritually unclean, and her remarriage would be an abomination in the Presence of God and defile the land with sin, this land that God, your God, is giving you as an inheritance.
MSG.5: When a man takes a new wife, he is not to go out with the army or be given any business or work duties. He gets one year off simply to be at home making his wife happy.
MSG.6: Don't seize a handmill or an upper millstone as collateral for a loan. You'd be seizing someone's very life.
MSG.7: If a man is caught kidnapping one of his kinsmen, someone of the People of Israel, to enslave or sell him, the kidnapper must die. Purge that evil from among you.
MSG.8: Warning! If a serious skin disease breaks out, follow exactly the rules set down by the Levitical priests. Follow them precisely as I commanded them.
MSG.9: Don't forget what God, your God, did to Miriam on your way out of Egypt.
MSG.10: When you make a loan of any kind to your neighbor, don't enter his house to claim his pledge.
MSG.11: Wait outside. Let the man to whom you made the pledge bring the pledge to you outside.
MSG.12: And if he is destitute, don't use his cloak as a bedroll;
MSG.13: return it to him at nightfall so that he can sleep in his cloak and bless you. In the sight of God, your God, that will be viewed as a righteous act.
MSG.14: Don't abuse a laborer who is destitute and needy, whether he is a fellow Israelite living in your land and in your city.
MSG.15: Pay him at the end of each workday; he's living from hand to mouth and needs it now. If you hold back his pay, he'll protest to God and you'll have sin on your books.
MSG.16: Parents shall not be put to death for their children, nor children for their parents. Each person shall be put to death for his own sin.
MSG.17: Make sure foreigners and orphans get their just rights. Don't take the cloak of a widow as security for a loan.
MSG.18: Don't ever forget that you were once slaves in Egypt and God, your God, got you out of there. I command you: Do what I'm telling you.
MSG.19: When you harvest your grain and forget a sheaf back in the field, don't go back and get it; leave it for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow so that God, your God, will bless you in all your work.
MSG.20: When you shake the olives off your trees, don't go back over the branches and strip them bare—what's left is for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow.
MSG.21: And when you cut the grapes in your vineyard, don't take every last grape—leave a few for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow.
MSG.22: Don't ever forget that you were a slave in Egypt. I command you: Do what I'm telling you.

NIV.1: If a man marries a woman who becomes displeasing to him because he finds something indecent about her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce, gives it to her and sends her from his house,
NIV.2: and if after she leaves his house she becomes the wife of another man,
NIV.3: and her second husband dislikes her and writes her a certificate of divorce, gives it to her and sends her from his house, or if he dies,
NIV.4: then her first husband, who divorced her, is not allowed to marry her again after she has been defiled. That would be detestable in the eyes of the Lord. Do not bring sin upon the land the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance.
NIV.5: If a man has recently married, he must not be sent to war or have any other duty laid on him. For one year he is to be free to stay at home and bring happiness to the wife he has married.
NIV.6: Do not take a pair of millstones—not even the upper one—as security for a debt, because that would be taking a man’s livelihood as security.
NIV.7: If a man is caught kidnapping one of his brother Israelites and treats him as a slave or sells him, the kidnapper must die. You must purge the evil from among you.
NIV.8: In cases of leprous diseases be very careful to do exactly as the priests, who are Levites, instruct you. You must follow carefully what I have commanded them.
NIV.9: Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam along the way after you came out of Egypt.
NIV.10: When you make a loan of any kind to your neighbor, do not go into his house to get what he is offering as a pledge.
NIV.11: Stay outside and let the man to whom you are making the loan bring the pledge out to you.
NIV.12: If the man is poor, do not go to sleep with his pledge in your possession.
NIV.13: Return his cloak to him by sunset so that he may sleep in it. Then he will thank you, and it will be regarded as a righteous act in the sight of the Lord your God.
NIV.14: Do not take advantage of a hired man who is poor and needy, whether he is a brother Israelite or an alien living in one of your towns.
NIV.15: Pay him his wages each day before sunset, because he is poor and is counting on it. Otherwise he may cry to the Lord against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
NIV.16: Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor children put to death for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin.
NIV.17: Do not deprive the alien or the fatherless of justice, or take the cloak of the widow as a pledge.
NIV.18: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and the Lord your God redeemed you from there. That is why I command you to do this.
NIV.19: When you are harvesting in your field and you overlook a sheaf, do not go back to get it. Leave it for the alien, the fatherless and the widow, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
NIV.20: When you beat the olives from your trees, do not go over the branches a second time. Leave what remains for the alien, the fatherless and the widow.
NIV.21: When you harvest the grapes in your vineyard, do not go over the vines again. Leave what remains for the alien, the fatherless and the widow.
NIV.22: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.

NET.1: If a man marries a woman and she does not please him because he has found something offensive in her, then he may draw up a divorce document, give it to her, and evict her from his house.
NET.2: When she has left him she may go and become someone else’s wife.
NET.3: If the second husband rejects her and then divorces her, gives her the papers, and evicts her from his house, or if the second husband who married her dies,
NET.4: her first husband who divorced her is not permitted to remarry her after she has become ritually impure, for that is offensive to the LORD. You must not bring guilt on the land which the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
NET.5: When a man is newly married, he need not go into the army nor be obligated in any way; he must be free to stay at home for a full year and bring joy to the wife he has married.
NET.6: One must not take either lower or upper millstones as security on a loan, for that is like taking a life itself as security.
NET.7: If a man is found kidnapping a person from among his fellow Israelites, and regards him as mere property and sells him, that kidnapper must die. In this way you will purge evil from among you.
NET.8: Be careful during an outbreak of leprosy to follow precisely all that the Levitical priests instruct you; as I have commanded them, so you should do.
NET.9: Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam along the way after you left Egypt.
NET.10: When you make any kind of loan to your neighbor, you may not go into his house to claim what he is offering as security.
NET.11: You must stand outside and the person to whom you are making the loan will bring out to you what he is offering as security.
NET.12: If the person is poor you may not use what he gives you as security for a covering.
NET.13: You must by all means return to him at sunset the item he gave you as security so that he may sleep in his outer garment and bless you for it; it will be considered a just deed by the LORD your God.
NET.14: You must not oppress a lowly and poor servant, whether one from among your fellow Israelites or from the resident foreigners who are living in your land and villages.
NET.15: You must pay his wage that very day before the sun sets, for he is poor and his life depends on it. Otherwise he will cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
NET.16: Fathers must not be put to death for what their children do, nor children for what their fathers do; each must be put to death for his own sin.
NET.17: You must not pervert justice due a resident foreigner or an orphan, or take a widow’s garment as security for a loan.
NET.18: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and that the LORD your God redeemed you from there; therefore I am commanding you to do all this.
NET.19: Whenever you reap your harvest in your field and leave some unraked grain there, you must not return to get it; it should go to the resident foreigner, orphan, and widow so that the LORD your God may bless all the work you do.
NET.20: When you beat your olive tree you must not repeat the procedure; the remaining olives belong to the resident foreigner, orphan, and widow.
NET.21: When you gather the grapes of your vineyard you must not do so a second time; they should go to the resident foreigner, orphan, and widow.
NET.22: Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt; therefore, I am commanding you to do all this.
